label: Brisnik: antidepressant with cognitive impairment or dementia
title: Any antidepressant in a person with cognitive impairment or dementia
statement: Prescribed any antidepressant - and the patient has cognitive impairment or dementia

source.document: Brisnik V, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: indicators of high-risk and overprescribing. BMC Med 2024;22:193, Tables 3-4

plain_summary: Antidepressants can add to confusion, drowsiness and falls in a person with memory problems. The need for the antidepressant should be reviewed.

medicine_groups.name: Antidepressants (any)
medicine_groups.note: All antidepressant classes count, at any dose: SSRI, SNRI, mirtazapine, tricyclics, trazodone, tranylcypromine, moclobemide, phenelzine, agomelatine, vortioxetine, reboxetine and mianserin. Bupropion sold for quitting smoking is not counted. Dosulepin is also called dothiepin. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.meets: A clinician documented cognitive impairment or dementia that was present during the antidepressant course.

options.words: A clinician documented cognitive impairment or dementia during this course
A clinician ruled out both conditions for this course
The condition began only after this course ended
Unknown during this course, or symptoms or a screening score only

rule_for_models: With a Group A supply, cite the supply and a diagnosis of cognitive impairment or dementia present during the course, even with a high screening score or an earlier normal assessment. Report no finding if a clinical assessment rules out both for that course or the condition began only after it ended. If diagnosis or timing is unclear, including symptoms or a screening score alone, report a possible finding and ask whether a clinician diagnosed either condition during the course.
cannot_be_seen: How severe the memory problem is, how the person is coping, and why the antidepressant was started. Medicines bought without a prescription or supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: If cognitive status is unclear, could you confirm whether cognitive impairment or dementia has been diagnosed? If present, could you review whether the antidepressant is still needed and helping?
